title: Surface Area and Volume of Cubes and Rectangular Prisms
seo_title: Grade 7 Surface Area and Volume Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 7: 4.2 Surface area and volume of 3D objects
standard_text: Use appropriate formulae to calculate the surface area, volume and capacity of cubes and rectangular prisms; describe the interrelationship between surface area and volume; solve problems involving surface area, volume and capacity; use and convert between appropriate SI units, including mm³, cm³ and m³, and mℓ, ℓ and kℓ.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 surface area and volume worksheets: volume and surface area of cubes and rectangular prisms, missing lengths and unit conversions. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Surface area: add all six faces.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Volume of a rectangular prism = length × breadth × height. Cube: V = l³.
  • Surface area = the total area of all the faces. Rectangular prism: 2(lb + lh + bh). Cube: 6l².
  • 1 cm³ = 1 mℓ; 1 000 cm³ = 1 ℓ; 1 m³ = 1 000 ℓ.
  • Volume is in cubic units (cm³); surface area is in square units (cm²).

Examples

Example

A box 10 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm

V = 10 × 6 × 4

SA = 2(60 + 40 + 24)

Answer: 240 cm³ and 248 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the lengthsMultiply length, breadth and height.
Three faces onlyA prism has 6 faces.
100 for cubic units1 cm³ = 1 000 mm³.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 7 say about surface area and volume?
faq.a: Calculate the surface area, volume and capacity of cubes and rectangular prisms, and convert between cubic units and capacity units.
All the faces you add for the surface area.

faq.q: Is volume the same as capacity?
faq.a: Capacity is how much a container holds; it is measured in ℓ.

items.q: Each small cube is 1 cm³. What is the volume of this prism?
items.e: Each layer has 2 rows of 4 cubes = 8 cubes. There are 2 layers: 8 × 2 = 16 cm³. Count the hidden cubes, too: only 13 cubes show a face.

items.q: A small box has a volume of 250 cm³. How many millilitres of water can it hold?
items.e: 1 cm³ holds exactly 1 mℓ. So 250 cm³ = 250 mℓ.

items.q: A cube-shaped container is 10 cm × 10 cm × 10 cm inside. How much water does it hold when full?
items.e: V = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1 000 cm³ = 1 000 mℓ = 1 ℓ. (10 × 10 = 100 is only the base, and 30 adds the edges.)

items.q: A jug has a volume of 3 500 cm³. How many litres does it hold?
A water tank holds 2 m³. How many litres is that?
items.e: 1 m³ = 100 cm × 100 cm × 100 cm = 1 000 000 cm³ = 1 000 ℓ. So 2 m³ = 2 000 ℓ. (2 000 000 is the number of mℓ, not L.)

items.q: Liam’s fish tank is 60 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many litres does it hold when full?
Liam fills the same fish tank (60 cm long, 30 cm wide, 40 cm high) only up to 35 cm. How much water is in it?
items.e: Use the height of the water, not the tank: 60 × 30 × 35 = 1 800 × 35 = 63 000 cm³ = 63 ℓ. 9 ℓ is the empty space at the top.

items.q: Anika builds a cedar planter box that is 120 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm deep inside. Soil comes in 50 ℓ bags. How many bags does she need to fill the box?
items.e: V = 120 × 40 × 30 = 144 000 cm³ = 144 ℓ. 144 ÷ 50 = 2,88, so 2 bags are not enough. She needs 3 bags.

items.q: A juice box is 6 cm long, 4 cm wide and 10 cm high. How much juice can it hold?
items.e: V = 6 × 4 × 10 = 240 cm³. 1 cm³ = 1 mℓ, so it holds 240 mℓ. (2,4 ℓ would be 2 400 mℓ.)

items.q: An aquarium has a base 50 cm long and 25 cm wide. Ethan pours in 25 ℓ of water. How deep is the water?
items.e: 25 ℓ = 25 000 cm³. Base area: 50 × 25 = 1 250 cm². Depth = 25 000 ÷ 1 250 = 20 cm. 500 divides by the length only.

items.q: A storage bin holds 60 ℓ. Its inside base is 50 cm long and 40 cm wide. How high is the inside of the bin?
items.e: 60 ℓ = 60 000 cm³. Base area: 50 × 40 = 2 000 cm². Height = 60 000 ÷ 2 000 = 30 cm. 1 200 divides by the length only.
